subject.title: fix: setup fails closed for invalid configuration arguments

question: Should valid legacy setup invocations that repeat a value option retain first-value-wins semantics, or is strict duplicate rejection an approved breaking SetupEngine CLI contract?
rationale: The strict parser is mechanically correct, but choosing whether existing automation should fail is a compatibility policy decision rather than a defect that an automated repair can safely resolve.

options.title: Preserve legacy duplicate handling
options.body: Keep first-value-wins for repeated value options while retaining fail-closed validation for missing, unknown, positional, and unreadable configuration input.

options.title: Approve strict duplicate rejection
options.body: Accept exit-code-2 failures for repeated value options and require prominent upgrade guidance plus focused compatibility proof for existing automation.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy duplicate handling
recommendation.body: Keep first-value-wins for repeated value options while retaining fail-closed validation for missing, unknown, positional, and unreadable configuration input.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current implementation and documentation changes and can route the explicit compatibility decision to the setup-area owner.
